newsitem.title: CHINA: China denies building missile plant in Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: China denies building missile plant in Pakistan.

text.p: China on Tuesday dismissed a CIA report that China had helped Pakistan build a factory to produce medium-range ballistic missiles.
"The report... is groundless," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai told a regular news briefing, when asked to comment on the report by Time Magazine.

Time said U.S. intelligence services discovered the facility near Rawalpindi in late 1995 and concluded that China was not only selling missiles to Pakistan but also helping the Pakistanis build a factory to manufacture them.
If confirmed, such a report could endanger the Clinton administrations's policy of extending Most Favoured Nation trading status to China, due to go to a vote on Tuesday in Congress.
President Bill Clinton has declined to comment on the report, saying he could not discuss "alleged intelligence reports".
China had promised in 1994 not to sell such sensitive military technology to other nations.

By late last summer, the CIA concluded that China had delivered to Pakistan not just missile parts but also 30 ready-to-launch M-11 missiles, each capable of carrying a 1,100-lb (500 kg) warhead more than 185 miles (297 km).
